findings.title: from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=...), sd) silently discards the template's budget; budget_exceeded then fails open forever
findings.claim: The Accountant serializer is registered with `lambda _template, sd: _accountant_from_state_dict(dict(sd))` (line 246) - the template is discarded entirely. `_accountant_state_dict` only writes a `budget` key when `acct._budget is not None` (line 226-227), and `_accountant_from_state_dict` sets `budget = None` unless the saved dict carries one (line 232-234). So `from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(...)), saved)` returns an Accountant whose `_budget` is None whenever the checkpoint was written by a run that had no budget (which is every DPTrainer checkpoint - `_dp_trainer.py:1535` constructs `Accountant()` with no budget). `Accountant.budget_exceeded` then hits `if self._budget is None: return False` (line 215-216) and returns False unconditionally, forever. The dispatcher's documented contract ('handlers may ignore it when the dict is self-describing', _dispatch.py:96-107) makes this a silent, by-design drop with no warning and no way for the caller to detect it short of reading `acct._budget` (a private attribute).
findings.failure_scenario: A two-stage run: stage 1 trains with a fixed `privacy_noise_multiplier` (no budget) and saves `accountant.json`. Stage 2 resumes with an explicit cap - `acct = from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)), json.load(f))` - and drives the documented stop loop `for step in ...: acct = acct | step; if acct.budget_exceeded: break`. Reproduced verbatim on the current tree: after 2000 composed Poisson(Gaussian(1.1), q=0.01) steps the restored accountant reports `epsilon_at(1e-5) = 2.1597`, `_budget = None`, `budget_exceeded = False`. The loop never breaks and the run continues past 2.16x its stated epsilon budget with no error, no warning, and no log line. The Accountant class docstring's own resume recipe (lines 73-87) happens to sidestep this by passing `prefix=sft.process` into a fresh `Accountant(budget=budget, ...)`, so the natural one-liner is exactly the unsafe form.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_accountant.py:243-247 -> `register_serializer(Accountant, _accountant_state_dict, lambda _template, sd: _accountant_from_state_dict(dict(sd)))` - `_template` is named with a leading underscore and never read.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_accountant.py:231-235 -> `budget = None; if "budget" in state: budget = budget_from_state_dict(...)` - a checkpoint with no budget key yields budget=None regardless of the template.
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_accountant.py:215-216 -> `if self._budget is None: return False` - the fail-open branch.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1535 -> `accounting = Accountant()` - DPTrainer never attaches a budget, so every trainer-written accountant.json lacks the key.

Repro (current tree, .venv): `state_dict(a)` -> keys ['process'] only; `b = from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)), sd)` -> `b.epsilon_at(1e-5)=2.159739`, `b._budget=None`, `b.budget_exceeded=False`.
findings.fix_sketch: Have the Accountant from_state_dict handler consult the template: when the saved dict has no `budget` key, keep `template._budget` instead of dropping it. Separately, make `budget_exceeded` distinguish 'no budget configured' from 'budget check unavailable' - e.g. raise (or return None / a tri-state) when the caller asked for a budget that could not be restored, and log at restore time whenever a template budget is being discarded.

findings.title: Four privacy-relevant kwargs dicts on TrainingArguments accept arbitrary keys silently; the three keys that are read are renames of the underlying public parameter names
findings.claim: `clipping_kwargs` is read at exactly one site: `ca = a.clipping_kwargs; target_clip_rate = float(ca.get("target_clipping_rate", 0.5)); clip_norm_max = float(ca.get("norm_max", 10.0)); auto_gamma = float(ca.get("gamma", 0.01))`. Every other key is silently discarded. Worse, the two adaptive-clipping keys are *renames* of the public parameters they feed: `target_clipping_rate` -> `adaptive_clipped_grad(target_quantile=...)` and `norm_max` -> `adaptive_clipped_grad(clipping_norm_max=...)`. A user who reads `opaque.dpsgd.adaptive_clipped_grad`'s signature (the documented mechanism API) and writes `clipping_kwargs={"target_quantile": 0.9, "clipping_norm_max": 50.0}` gets a silent no-op. `adaptive_clipped_grad`'s remaining knobs (`learning_rate`, `clipping_norm_min`, `fraction_noise_std`) are unreachable from the trainer at all, and passing them is also silent. The same no-validation pattern applies to `sampling_kwargs` (only `truncated_batch_size`/`max_batch_size`/`total_participations` are ever read), `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs` on the gaussian path (filtered to exactly `("bound", "compute_dtype")` at `_dp_trainer.py:1544-1552`), and `noise_calibration_kwargs` (only `min`/`max`/`tolerance`). The same class validates `lr_scheduler_kwargs` strictly - `_scheduler.py:83-91` raises `ValueError` listing the allowed keys - so the inconsistency is internal, not a house style.
findings.failure_scenario: A user wants adaptive clipping at the 90th percentile with a higher ceiling and configures `TrainingArguments(clipping_mode='adaptive', clipping_kwargs={'target_quantile': 0.9, 'clipping_norm_max': 50.0})`. Construction succeeds with no error and no warning (verified: `a.clipping_kwargs` round-trips the dict untouched). Training runs at `target_quantile=0.5` and `clipping_norm_max=10.0` - a materially different clipping schedule from the one requested, discoverable only by reading the trainer source. Same class of failure for `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bounds': (-1.0, 1.0)}` (plural typo of `bound`): accepted, normalized to a list, and dropped by the `_k in ("bound", "compute_dtype")` filter, so an unbounded Gaussian is deployed while the user believes the bounded mechanism is in effect.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4145-4148 -> the only three `ca.get(...)` reads; `grep -n 'clipping_kwargs' _dp_trainer.py` returns line 4145 and nothing else.

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py (public signature) -> `adaptive_clipped_grad(..., target_quantile=0.5, clipping_norm_max=100.0, learning_rate=0.2, clipping_norm_min=0.01, fraction_noise_std=0.05, ...)` - the names the trainer renames or omits.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1544-1552 -> `_gn_extra = {_k: _v for ... if _k in ("bound", "compute_dtype")}` - silent filter on privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs.
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_scheduler.py:83-91 -> `_validate_kwargs` raises on unsupported `lr_scheduler_kwargs` keys, showing the intended pattern.

Repro (current tree): `TrainingArguments(output_dir='/tmp/x', privacy_noise_multiplier=1.0, clipping_mode='adaptive', clipping_kwargs={'target_quantile':0.9,'clipping_norm_max':50.0,'fraction_noise_std':0.5,'learning_rate':0.9,'typo_knob':1})` constructs with zero warnings and keeps all five keys verbatim.
Repro: `noise_calibration_kwargs={'minimum': 0.5}` -> normalized to `{'minimum': 0.5, 'min': 0.11, 'max': 10.0, 'tolerance': 0.001}` - the typo sits alongside the defaults it was meant to replace.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an allow-list validator per dict (mirroring `_scheduler._validate_kwargs`) in `TrainingArguments._validate_privacy_fields`, keyed by `clipping_mode` / `sampling_mode` / `privacy_noise_mechanism`, raising `ValueError` with the accepted key set. Prefer keeping the underlying public parameter names (`target_quantile`, `clipping_norm_max`) rather than renaming them, or accept both and document the alias.

findings.title: per_group() silently drops patterns that match no parameter, so a typo'd or model-mismatched group name degrades to the fallback clip norm with no signal
findings.claim: `per_group` validates in one direction only. It raises when a parameter matches zero patterns (line 129-136, but only when `fallback is None`) and when a parameter matches two or more (line 137-142), yet a *pattern* that matches zero parameters is silently removed: `values = {pat: float(val) for pat, val in all_patterns.items() if pat in used_groups}`. When `fallback` is supplied - which the trainer's dict form makes mandatory (`clipping_norm` dict 'must include a fallback key', verified by construction) - a misspelled or model-inappropriate substring produces no error, no warning, and no trace in the returned `PerGroup`: the affected parameters just get the fallback bound. The docstring's Raises section enumerates the three checks that do exist and never mentions this case, so the omission also is not documented behavior a reader could rely on.
findings.failure_scenario: A user configures tighter clipping on attention with `per_group(params, self_atten=0.1, mlp=2.0, fallback=1.0)` (typo: `self_atten` for `self_attn`). Reproduced on the current tree with LLaMA-shaped names: the returned PerGroup is `groups={('...mlp.up_proj.weight',): 'mlp', ('...self_attn.q_proj.weight',): 'fallback'}`, `values={'mlp': 2.0, 'fallback': 1.0}` - the attention parameters are clipped at 1.0 (10x the intended 0.1) and the `self_atten` entry has vanished. Same for a pattern set copied from another architecture: `per_group(params, q_proj=0.1, k_proj=0.1, v_proj=0.1, fallback=1.0)` against a model with fused QKV yields `values={'q_proj': 0.1, 'fallback': 1.0}` - two of the three requested groups silently gone. Because the accountant reads the realized PerGroup, epsilon stays self-consistent; the damage is a silently different clipping (and per-group noise allocation) than the one the user wrote down.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:146-149 -> `values = {pat: float(val) for pat, val in all_patterns.items() if pat in used_groups}` - unmatched patterns filtered out, no error path.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:129-142 -> the two checks that DO raise, both on the parameter side.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py docstring 'Raises:' block -> lists 'no patterns provided', 'parameter matches zero patterns (and no fallback)', 'parameter matches multiple patterns', 'value is not positive' - the unmatched-pattern case is absent.

Repro (current tree): `per_group({'model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight': t, 'model.layers.0.mlp.up_proj.weight': t}, self_atten=0.1, mlp=2.0, fallback=1.0)` -> `values == {'mlp': 2.0, 'fallback': 1.0}`; the q_proj leaf is assigned group 'fallback'.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py `_coerce_clipping_norm` -> rejects a `clipping_norm` dict without a 'fallback' key, so the trainer path always runs in the mode where this check is disabled.
findings.fix_sketch: Raise `ValueError` listing the patterns that matched no leaf (with a few sample display paths to make the mismatch diagnosable), or at minimum emit a `RuntimeWarning`. An opt-out kwarg (`allow_unused_patterns=True`) covers the legitimate 'one config across several architectures' case.

findings.title: compute_loss_func is silently ignored on the default eval path, so eval_loss and best-model selection measure a different objective than training
findings.claim: `DPTrainer.__init__` stores `compute_loss_func` (line 467) and honours it in `compute_per_example_loss` (line 2320-2322). `prediction_step` reaches that method only when `use_per_example_loss` is true, which requires `"loss" in (self.args.include_for_metrics or [])` (line 2485-2488). `TrainingArguments.include_for_metrics` defaults to an empty list (`_training_arguments.py:364`, `field(default_factory=list)`), so on the default configuration evaluation takes the batched branch and reads the model's own loss directly: `loss = output.get("loss")` (line 2571). No warning is emitted on that branch when `_compute_loss_func` is not None - the only nearby warning (line 2535-2541) fires in the opposite direction. This diverges from `transformers.Trainer`, whose `prediction_step` routes through `compute_loss`, which does apply `compute_loss_func`.
findings.failure_scenario: A user passes `compute_loss_func=my_weighted_ce` together with `eval_strategy='steps'`, `metric_for_best_model='eval_loss'`, `greater_is_better=False`, `load_best_model_at_end=True` - all fields the class supports. Training minimizes `my_weighted_ce`; the reported `eval_loss` is the HF model's built-in `ForCausalLMLoss`. Checkpoint selection, early-stopping callbacks, and any logged eval curve are therefore driven by an objective the user never asked for, silently. The same branch also skips the `label_smoothing_factor` rebuild that `compute_per_example_loss` applies (line 2299-2340), so `label_smoothing_factor > 0` is likewise absent from the reported eval loss.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2485-2488 -> `use_per_example_loss = ("loss" in (self.args.include_for_metrics or []) and has_labels and not prediction_loss_only)`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:364 -> `include_for_metrics: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)` - default is empty, so the per-example branch is off by default.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2571 -> batched branch: `loss = output.get("loss")`; `grep -n '_compute_loss_func' _dp_trainer.py` returns only lines 467, 2320, 2322 - it is never consulted on this path.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2550-2555 -> the comment acknowledges it ('users who want compute_loss_func honoured at eval set include_for_metrics=["loss"]') but the code emits no runtime warning.
findings.fix_sketch: In `prediction_step`, when `self._compute_loss_func is not None` and the batched branch is taken, either route the batched output through `compute_loss_func` (it already receives `(outputs, labels)`) or emit a one-shot `RuntimeWarning` naming `include_for_metrics=['loss']` as the opt-in. Silent divergence between the trained and the reported objective should not be the default.

findings.title: set_discretization is a full replace, not a partial update: tuning one knob silently reverts every previously tightened Monte Carlo / grid parameter
findings.claim: `set_discretization` takes eight parameters, all with library defaults, and assigns `_default_config = DiscretizationConfig(<all eight>)` unconditionally (lines 145-154). It does not read the existing `_default_config`, so any parameter the caller omits is reset to the library default rather than preserved. The docstring calls it 'Set module-level default discretization parameters' and its own worked example - `acc.set_discretization(discretization=1e-3)` (line 132-133) - is exactly the single-knob call shape that silently undoes prior settings. Three of the eight parameters (`discretization`, `mc_resolution`, `mc_failure_probability`) directly move the reported epsilon, and the last two govern the simultaneous confidence band that the b-min-sep and balls-in-bins accountants use - the auto-paired samplers for 5 of the 6 MF mechanisms in `_SAMPLER_BY_MECHANISM`.
findings.failure_scenario: A team tightens the Monte Carlo band for a DP-FTRL run: `acc.set_discretization(mc_failure_probability=1e-10, mc_resolution=1e-8)`. Later, in the same process (or in a shared setup module), someone coarsens the grid for speed: `acc.set_discretization(discretization=1e-3)`. Reproduced on the current tree: the resulting config is `mc_resolution=1e-05, mc_failure_probability=1e-06` - both silently back at the library defaults, four orders of magnitude looser on the failure probability. Every epsilon computed afterwards is certified at a weaker confidence level than the team configured, with no warning and no diff in any artifact they inspect.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/discretization.py:145-154 -> `global _default_config; _default_config = DiscretizationConfig(discretization=discretization, ..., mc_failure_probability=mc_failure_probability)` - constructed from the arguments alone, existing state never read.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/discretization.py:132-133 -> docstring example `acc.set_discretization(discretization=1e-3)`, the partial-looking call that triggers the reset.

Repro (current tree): `acc.set_discretization(mc_failure_probability=1e-10, mc_resolution=1e-8)` -> config shows `mc_resolution=1e-08, mc_failure_probability=1e-10`; then `acc.set_discretization(discretization=1e-3)` -> config shows `discretization=0.001, mc_resolution=1e-05, mc_failure_probability=1e-06`.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/discretization.py:36-38 -> `mc_resolution` / `mc_failure_probability` are the Monte Carlo confidence-band parameters; `get_discretization` (keyword-only) is asymmetric with `set_discretization` (positional-or-keyword), reinforcing the impression that the setter is an override rather than a replace.
findings.fix_sketch: Give every parameter a `None` sentinel and merge onto the current `_default_config` (matching `get_discretization`'s override semantics), or rename to `replace_discretization` / add an explicit `update_discretization`. Making the parameters keyword-only would also match `get_discretization`.

findings.title: is_runtime_patched() returns True even when zero runtime patches were installed - the documented safety predicate for non-DPTrainer flows fails open
findings.claim: `apply_runtime_patches` sets the module global `_runtime_patches_applied = True` on line 102, before attempting any patch. Each of the four patch installs is wrapped in `try: ... except ImportError:` and three of them (`vmap_masking`, `vmap_grouped_mm`, `empty_batches`) swallow the failure with a bare `pass` - no log, no warning, no record. `is_runtime_patched()` (line 159) returns that global. Its docstring explicitly positions it as the check a non-trainer script uses ('lets a script that drives HF primitives without DPTrainer check whether the global shims are installed'), and AGENTS.md prescribes exactly that flow, so the predicate is consumed as a safety gate but reports installation intent rather than installation.
findings.failure_scenario: `pip install opaque-patches` without the `[transformers]` extra (a documented installation option). A script calls `apply_runtime_patches()`; all three transformers-side imports raise ImportError and are swallowed silently, the checkpoint patch logs a warning. `is_runtime_patched()` then returns True and a script gated on it proceeds to run `vmap(grad(...))` with none of the vmap-safety shims (vmap-safe causal-mask builders, the Poisson empty-batch collator handling, the gradient-checkpointing shim) actually in place. Reproduced on the current tree by blocking the patch-module imports: `is_runtime_patched() -> True` while `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint.__module__` is still `torch.utils.checkpoint` (unpatched) and no masking/collator/MoE patch was installed.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:101-102 -> `global _runtime_patches_applied` / `_runtime_patches_applied = True` at the top of the function, before any patch attempt.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:110-137 -> three `except ImportError: pass` blocks (masking, grouped_mm, collator) with no logging.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:152-159 -> `is_runtime_patched` docstring and `return _runtime_patches_applied`.

Repro (current tree): with `builtins.__import__` blocking `opaque.api.patches.transformers*` and `opaque.api.patches.torch`, `apply_runtime_patches()` logged only the checkpoint warning, then `P.is_runtime_patched()` -> True and `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint.__module__` -> 'torch.utils.checkpoint' (no patch applied).

AGENTS.md 'Patching model (on-import)' -> 'non-trainer flows should call opaque.patches.apply_runtime_patches() once plus opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(model)' - the flow the predicate exists to guard.
findings.fix_sketch: Track which patches actually installed and set the flag from that, e.g. `_installed: set[str]`, with `is_runtime_patched()` returning True only when the requested concerns all landed (and an `installed_runtime_patches()` accessor for detail). At minimum, log a warning on each swallowed ImportError instead of `pass`, and reflect partial installation in the predicate.

findings.title: BandMfStrategy alone drops min_sep / max_participations into a **_ kwargs sink - the only two arguments in the MfStrategy protocol that carry the participation assumption its amplification depends on
findings.claim: The `MfStrategy` protocol is called with the participation context - `CyclicPoisson.pld_at` does `sensitivity = s.sensitivity(n_steps=self.n_steps, min_sep=self.min_sep, max_participations=self.max_participations)` (_poisson.py:180-184). `BsrStrategy`, `BisrStrategy`, `BltStrategy` and `LambdaCgdStrategy` all declare those parameters explicitly and feed them into their sensitivity math. `BandMfStrategy` declares `def sensitivity(self, *, n_steps: int, **_) -> float` (line 128) and `def streaming_matrix(self, *, n_steps: int, **_)` (line 125) and `def coefficients(self, *, n_steps: int, **_)` (line 112) - min_sep and max_participations vanish into `**_`. Concretely, `band_mf_strategy(bands=16).sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=1, max_participations=1000)` returns 0.9999999999999999, bit-identical to `.sensitivity(n_steps=1000)`: the worst-possible participation pattern (every step, no separation) produces the single-participation column norm. Correspondingly `CyclicPoisson.min_sep` returns the degenerate 1 with the comment 'BandMF or Identity (which ignore it)' (_poisson.py:87-95). NOTE: the downstream consequence - `privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band'` with `sampling_mode='poisson'` deploying a plain PoissonSampler against `ceil(n_steps/bands)`-group cyclic accounting - is already reported (sweep-horizon-prefix.json, sweep-docs-drift.json) and tracked by open #320 / #356 / #359. What is reported here is the distinct code-level mechanism: the one signal in the strategy protocol that could have flagged the mismatch is a kwargs sink, and it is a sink on the *public* `opaque.dpftrl` surface, not just inside the trainer.
findings.failure_scenario: A library user (no DPTrainer) writes the pairing themselves: `proc = ftrl_acc.poisson(ftrl_acc.mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=16)), sample_rate=0.01, n_steps=1000)` - which is verbatim the worked example in `poisson()`'s own docstring (_poisson.py:282-287) - and drives it with `opaque.dpsgd.PoissonSampler(dataset, 0.01, n_steps=1000, key=k)`, which offers no min-separation. Measured on the current tree: that process reports `epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.6231`, versus `1.8282` for the same noise multiplier and sample rate with `identity_strategy()` (plain DP-SGD) - a ~2.9x reduction obtained purely from the banded decomposition, which is valid only under >= 16-min-separated participation. Nothing in the API surface - not `band_mf_strategy`, not `poisson()`, not the strategy protocol - refuses the combination or even records what separation the reported number assumes.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_band_mf.py:128-130 -> `def sensitivity(self, *, n_steps: int, **_) -> float: coefs = self.coefficients(n_steps=n_steps); return float(coefs.norm())`.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_bsr.py:169-171, _bisr.py:232-234, _lambda_cgd.py:171-173, _blt.py:174-176 -> every other strategy declares `min_sep` / `max_participations` and uses them.
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:180-184 -> the call site that passes min_sep/max_participations into the sink.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:87-95 -> `min_sep` property returns 1 with 'Cyclic Poisson provides no worst-case separation guarantee ... this value only ever shows up for BandMF or Identity (which ignore it)'.

Measured (current tree): `band_mf_strategy(bands=16).sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=1, max_participations=1000) == .sensitivity(n_steps=1000) == 0.9999999999999999`; `ftrl_acc.poisson(mf_gaussian(1.0, band16), 0.01, n_steps=1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.6231` vs identity 1.8282.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `**_` with explicit `min_sep: int` / `max_participations: int | None` on `BandMfStrategy.sensitivity` and have it raise when `min_sep < self.bands` (the precondition of the banded decomposition), rather than silently returning the single-participation norm. That turns the `mf_band` + `sampling_mode='poisson'` pairing and the equivalent hand-written pairing into loud failures at accountant-construction time.

findings.title: The shipped opaque.accounting module docstring names seven accounting factories that do not exist and omits four that do
findings.claim: The package facade's module docstring - what `help(opaque.accounting)` and the generated API reference render - directs users to `opaque.dpsgd.accounting` for `gaussian, adaclip, poisson, truncated_poisson, parallel_poisson` and to `opaque.dpftrl.accounting` for `band_mf, blt, bisr, bsr, lambda_cgd, identity_mf, poisson, b_min_sep, balls_in_bins`. Verified against the installed packages: `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.__all__ == ['adaclip','gaussian','k_out_of_t','parallel_poisson','poisson','random_allocation']` (no `truncated_poisson`; `k_out_of_t` and `random_allocation` are undocumented here) and `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.__all__ == ['b_min_sep','balls_in_bins','mf_gaussian','per_step','poisson']` - six of the nine names listed are absent, and the one factory that actually builds every MF mechanism, `mf_gaussian(nm, strategy)`, is not mentioned. This is the migration residue of the move to the `mf_gaussian(nm, strategy)` form. (A sibling instance of the same drift in `docs/` was already reported by sweep-docs-drift.json; this is the shipped source docstring, a separate file and a separate discovery surface for anyone reading the installed package.)
findings.failure_scenario: A user following `help(opaque.accounting)` writes `import opaque.dpftrl.accounting as ftrl_acc; proc = ftrl_acc.blt(nm, ...)` and gets `AttributeError: module 'opaque.dpftrl.accounting' has no attribute 'blt'`, with no pointer to the real entry point `ftrl_acc.mf_gaussian(nm, blt_strategy(...))`. The failure is loud, so the cost is discovery friction rather than a wrong result - but it is the primary in-package map of the accounting surface and it is wrong for six of the nine DP-FTRL names it lists.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py:9-13 -> the two bullet lists.
Verified (current tree): `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.__all__ == ['adaclip','gaussian','k_out_of_t','parallel_poisson','poisson','random_allocation']`, `hasattr(dpsgd_acc,'truncated_poisson') == False`.

findings.title: build_strategy silently discards privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs for mf_identity while every other mechanism raises TypeError on an unknown key
findings.claim: `build_strategy` short-circuits on `mf_identity`: `if mechanism == "mf_identity": return factory()` (line 109-110), dropping the caller's `kwargs` entirely. For every other mechanism the function ends in `return factory(**extra)` (line 118), so an unknown key surfaces as a `TypeError` from the strategy factory. The result is that the same user error - a mistyped or mechanism-inappropriate key in `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs` - is loud for five of the six MF mechanisms and silent for the sixth.
findings.failure_scenario: A user experimenting with DP-FTRL sets `privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_identity'` while leaving over a `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bands': 8}` from an earlier `mf_band` config. Under `mf_band` that key is meaningful; under `mf_identity` it is silently dropped and the run proceeds with the plain identity strategy, so the user believes they are still running a banded mechanism. Switching the mechanism string back and forth therefore has an asymmetric error surface: `mf_band` -> `mf_identity` is silent, `mf_identity` -> `mf_band` with an identity-shaped kwargs dict raises.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:108-118 -> `factory = _STRATEGY_FACTORIES[mechanism]; if mechanism == "mf_identity": return factory(); extra = dict(kwargs) if kwargs else {}; ...; return factory(**extra)`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:213 -> `_MECH_DEFAULTS['mf_identity'] = {}` - nothing is pre-merged for this mechanism, so any key present came from the user.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:1078-1081 -> `_MECH_DEFAULTS[...]` keys are `setdefault`-merged into `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs`, and the docstring states the keys 'match the strategy factory signatures ... exactly so the trainer can spread the dict into the factory call' - the mf_identity branch breaks that contract.
findings.fix_sketch: Drop the special case and let `identity_strategy()` be called through the same `factory(**extra)` path, so a non-empty kwargs dict raises `TypeError` like every other mechanism; or raise an explicit `ValueError` naming the unexpected keys when `mechanism == 'mf_identity'` and `kwargs` is non-empty.

findings.title: with_restarts reuses the name transition_steps for the total span across all cycles, silently double-specifying the length against the base schedule it wraps
findings.claim: In every base factory in `opaque.scheduling` (`linear_schedule`, `cosine_schedule`, `polynomial_schedule`, ...) `transition_steps` is the length of one decay. In `with_warmup` it is the warmup length. In `with_restarts` it is the *total* span of all cycles, and the per-cycle length is the derived `transition_steps / num_cycles` (line 39). The wrapper never compares that derived cycle length to the inner schedule's own `transition_steps`, so a mismatch is silent: the inner schedule is simply evaluated over a truncated (or over-extended) domain, and past the total span `WithRestarts` returns the constant `self.schedule(cycle_length)` (line 43-44). The trainer builds the pair correctly (`_scheduler.py:200-215` constructs a `CosineSchedule` with `transition_steps = decay_steps / cycles` before wrapping), which is exactly the coupling a direct caller has to rediscover.
findings.failure_scenario: A user writes the natural composition `with_restarts(cosine_schedule(1.0, 0.0, transition_steps=1000), transition_steps=1000, num_cycles=4)` expecting four 1000-step cosine cycles. They get four 250-step windows in which the cosine traverses only the first 25% of its curve (LR never falls below ~0.96 of peak), and from step 1000 onward a flat `schedule(250)`. Reproduced with a linear base: `with_restarts(linear_schedule(1.0, 0.0, transition_steps=10), transition_steps=5, num_cycles=3)` yields [1.0, 0.9, 0.967, 0.867, 0.933, then 0.833 forever] - neither a restart pattern nor a decay. No error, no warning; the run just trains at a near-constant LR.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/scheduling/_with_restarts.py:39 -> `cycle_length = self.transition_steps / self.num_cycles` - transition_steps is the total span.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/scheduling/_with_restarts.py:43-44 -> `if relative >= self.transition_steps: return self.schedule(cycle_length)` - constant tail.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/scheduling/_with_restarts.py:61-70 -> the factory validates only `num_cycles > 0` and `transition_steps > 0`; it never inspects the wrapped schedule.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_scheduler.py:200-215 -> the trainer explicitly builds `CosineSchedule(transition_steps=decay_steps / cycles)` before `with_restarts(inner, transition_steps=decay_steps, num_cycles=cycles)`, with a comment that the inner half-cosine 'must span the *same* fractional length'.
Repro (current tree): `[round(float(with_restarts(linear_schedule(1.0,0.0,10), 5, 3)(i)),3) for i in range(16)]` -> [1.0, 0.9, 0.967, 0.867, 0.933, 0.833, 0.833, ...].
findings.fix_sketch: Either rename the wrapper parameter to `total_steps` (or `cycle_length` with an explicit per-cycle meaning), or have `with_restarts` accept `cycle_length` and derive the span; and, when the wrapped object is a recipe dataclass carrying its own `transition_steps`, warn (or raise) when it differs from `transition_steps / num_cycles`.

No missing/dangling __all__ entries: every listed name resolves. Umbrella distribution checked against reality - root pyproject.toml deps (opaque-engine/accounting/dpsgd/optimizers/patches) plus extras auditing/dpftrl/alignment/transformers/trl, and `opaque[all]` fans out to all of them; opaque-base arrives transitively via opaque-engine; no sub-package ships an opaque/__init__.py.

Sensitivity propagation through clipping -> noise: ran clipped_grad with normalize_by=1.0 and 2.0 and confirmed ClippedPytree.max_norm scales to 1.0 / 0.5 and gaussian_noise emits noise_stddev 1.1 / 0.55 accordingly. The normalize_by foot-gun (clipping divides but noise does not follow) does not exist here.

PerGroup / pytree identity: a PerGroup compiled from a flat named_parameters dict and applied to a nested params pytree fails closed with an exact diagnostic ('PerGroup path keys must match the pytree tensor leaves exactly. Leaves with no group assignment: ... Group paths with no matching leaf: ...'). per_group also raises correctly on a leaf matching zero patterns without fallback, on a leaf matching >=2 patterns, on non-positive values, and on non-tensor leaves. Only the unmatched-pattern direction is unguarded (reported).

calibrate() fails closed: read calibration.py:340-490 end to end. It raises on NaN at the bounds, on inf at both bounds, on a flat metric, on a bracket where neither endpoint is privacy-safe, on a bracket where both are, on a non-monotone interior probe outside the endpoint envelope, and on max_iterations exhaustion; convergence is only ever accepted from the proven privacy-safe endpoint. CalibrateResult.converged is documented and observed to be always True on return. The trainer's default noise_calibration bracket [0.11, 10.0] therefore raises rather than silently clamping when the target epsilon is unreachable.

PLD cache keying vs discretization: _pld_cache._CacheKey is (DiscretizationConfig, structural key, n_steps) and get_or_compute keys on it, so changing discretization computes a distinct PLD instead of returning a stale cached one. cached()/CachedProcess forward every discretization override to the inner process.

TrainingArguments domain validation: exercised the constructor with clipping_norm as '1.5', a JSON-object string, a dict without 'fallback', -1.0, 0.0, 'abc'; and microbatch_size 64-with-batch-8 and 0. All raise ValueError with the correct knob named. eval_strategy/logging_strategy/save_strategy/log_level/include_num_input_tokens_seen/clipping_mode/privacy_noise_mechanism/sampling_mode are all domain-checked; sampling_mode is additionally cross-checked against _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS per mechanism; sampling_kwargs rejects the privacy-owned keys {bands, sampling_prob}; k_out_of_t requires total_participations; truncated_batch_size/max_batch_size are rejected outside poisson; ignore_data_skip is restricted to cursor-free samplers. privacy_noise_multiplier=0.0 with a target epsilon, and clipping_norm=inf with a nonzero multiplier, both raise.

DPTrainer constructor accept-and-ignore check: `optimizers=(opt, sched)` raises ('Passing `optimizers` is not supported by DPTrainer'), `optimizer_cls_and_kwargs` is routed through validate_functional_optimizer_cls_and_kwargs, data_collator / processing_class / callbacks / preprocess_logits_for_metrics are all stored and consumed. Only compute_loss_func has a silent-ignore path (reported).

HF/TRL converter manifest engine (_convert.py::_apply_manifest): every source field must land in exactly one of DIRECT/RENAME/TRANSFORM/REJECT/DROP, and an unclassified *user-set* field raises rather than being dropped - the correct fail-closed shape for a migration seam. _normalize_dp_overrides requires one of privacy_noise_multiplier / privacy_target_epsilon, and typo'd override names propagate into cls(**converted) as a TypeError. The batch collapse correctly folds gradient_accumulation_steps into the logical Poisson batch (privacy-relevant) and maps HF per-device size to microbatch_size. _warmup_collapse and TrainingArguments.warmup_steps agree on the 5.x fractional-below-1 convention, and _scheduler.get_warmup_steps implements it.

lr_scheduler_kwargs is the one kwargs dict in TrainingArguments with strict per-scheduler key validation (_scheduler._validate_kwargs raises listing allowed keys); min_lr/min_lr_rate mutual exclusion, unknown scheduler names, and Schedule-recipe-plus-warmup_steps conflicts all raise. The trainer's with_warmup composition is HF-correct (decay built with transition_begin=W, then multiplied by the ramp).

opaque.distributed.sync fails closed on an unregistered type with the registered-type list in the message; the registry picks up AdaptiveClipState, GaussianNoiseState, MFNoiseState, SecondMomentMFNoiseState, the clip states, the aux types, and every optimizer state once the owning wheels are imported. reduce_pytree/reduce_pytree_/sum_gradients are wrapper-aware (ClippedPytree in -> ClippedPytree out, NoisedPytree preserved).

opaque.random key algebra: fold_in is a blake2b mix of (seed, value) and does change .seed, so the documented per-rank `fold_in(key, rank)` derivation the samplers rely on is real; split(k, n) is exactly the integer folds, as documented; int/str fold paths are separated; type errors on bool/non-int-non-str are raised.

opaque.serialization dispatcher: an unrecognised non-container leaf raises TypeError rather than being dropped; handler exceptions get an add_note naming the failing key path; resolve_serializer walks __mro__ so tensor subclasses reach the base handler; the Accountant handler fails closed with KeyError('process') on an empty or mis-keyed dict. The one gap is the discarded template (reported).

opaque.pytree: merge is last-wins and round-trips partition; partition returns two structurally disjoint trees with no None placeholders; global_norm promotes dtypes for the norm computation; tree_flatten_with_paths / param_path_display agree with what per_group matches against.

DPO loss configuration (opaque.transformers.trl): DPOConfig.__post_init__ validates loss_type/loss_weights length equality, rejects duplicate heads in an MPO list (which would silently collapse in the name-keyed parts dict), rejects sync_ref_model with an all-reference-free loss_type, enforces the robust/exo_pair label_smoothing preconditions, and builds _heads eagerly so an unknown loss_type raises at construction. chosen_nll's deliberate *_args/**_kwargs sink is correctly special-cased at the dispatch site (_dpo_trainer.py:932-933 passes chosen_logp, not the log-ratio), so the accept-and-ignore signature is not reachable with the wrong argument.
